top_categories.workout_context: 1340 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
At Race Around Ireland, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
72,178ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
54ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Race Around Ireland's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before race day.
1340 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 72,178ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Race Around Ireland's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 1340 miles.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 1340 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Race Around Ireland. Train it until it feels boring.
Low-cadence force work for 72,178ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.
72,178ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.

race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 1340 miles requires a practiced resupply plan built around confirmed course services and available commercial stops. Rehearse frequent carbohydrate intake on long rides, then scale the plan to intensity, sleep strategy, tolerance, and real food across the full event. Carry redundant fuel and avoid applying a short-event hourly target or fixed total-calorie estimate to a multi-day race.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Over Under, and Mixed Climbing to prepare you for 1340 miles of mixed terrain in Trim, County Meath, Ireland.
